title: Government to invest 4.7 trillion won in 'Frontier AI Development' next year
key_facts: South Korea's science ministry plans 4.7 trillion won next year for 'Frontier AI' development (budget proposal of 1 Sep).
Breakdown: 3.9 trillion won for 10,000 'Vera Rubin' GPUs, 800 billion for AI training data, 25 billion to attract 20 top overseas researchers.
Second Vice Minister Ryoo Jaemyung said at a briefing on the 2nd that the 'Dokpamo' independent AI foundation model project 'is by no means being stopped'.
Dokpamo's third-stage evaluation, due by mid-February, will pick two final teams, who keep GPU support.
Frontier AI is a separate project open to large firms, SMEs and startups; selection of investment candidates could start February or March.
Ryoo said the arrival of 'Mythos' in April moved the AI economy to a different level; a detailed plan follows the National Assembly's December budget.
quote_evidence: "The Dokpamo project is by no means being stopped."
"Since the emergence of Mythos in April, the AI economy has moved to a completely different level."

Specifically, 3.9 trillion won is earmarked for the purchase of 10,000 "Vera Rubin" GPUs, 800 billion won for the acquisition of AI training data, and 25 billion won to attract 20 top overseas researchers.
why_it_matters_hint: Korea splits its sovereign AI effort into two tracks amid doubts over whether the first was being dropped.
event_date: 2 Oct 2026 briefing (month assumed from publication date)
